research_question: Among young people aged up to 25 years in education settings who already show early signs or symptoms of suicide risk (such as suicidal ideation or a history of self-harm), what is the effect of indicated interventions, compared with control conditions, on suicidal ideation measured immediately at the end of the intervention?
treatment_label: Indicated interventions for young people with existing suicidal ideation, self-harm history, or other early suicide-risk symptoms in education settings
control_label: Control conditions (including usual care, waitlist, no intervention, attention control, or another eligible non-indicated comparator)
outcome_description: Suicidal ideation measured immediately postintervention, at the end of the intervention only. Exclude suicidal ideation measurements reported at short-term follow-up (1–3 months), medium-term follow-up (4–12 months), or the longest follow-up. Accept validated continuous ideation scales and quantitative dichotomous indicators of suicidal ideation. For multi-arm trials with multiple eligible indicated-intervention arms and one shared control, extract each eligible intervention-versus-control contrast as a separate row without merging or discarding intervention arms; preserve the shared-control linkage and account for dependence during synthesis (for example, with multilevel/robust methods or another appropriate shared-control adjustment). If a randomized study reports only the total sample size and gives no group-specific allocation, assume an even allocation across randomized groups unless otherwise stated, and explicitly flag this as an imputed 50/50 (or equal multi-group) allocation assumption.
positive_direction: A positive effect means the indicated intervention produced a greater reduction in suicidal ideation at immediate postintervention than the control condition.
search_queries: suicidal ideation indicated intervention students controlled trial
self-harm suicide risk intervention school university experiment
youth suicidal ideation education setting intervention quantitative outcome
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies of young people up to age 25 in school, college, university, or other education settings who already show suicidal ideation, self-harm history, or comparable early signs or symptoms of suicide risk, and who receive an indicated intervention.

Studies including a control or comparator condition and reporting suicidal ideation immediately at the end of the intervention; mixed samples or settings may be included when eligible participant or education-setting data are separately extractable.

Studies reporting sufficient quantitative information for an intervention-versus-control effect size at immediate postintervention, regardless of publication status, intervention format, or specific suicidal-ideation instrument.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study; exclude systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers.
No comparison between an indicated-intervention condition and a control or comparator condition.
No quantitative immediate-postintervention suicidal-ideation outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means and standard deviations, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios.

Completely unrelated to indicated suicide-risk interventions for symptomatic young people in education settings, including universal interventions delivered regardless of risk and selective interventions for at-risk but not yet symptomatic groups when no eligible indicated subgroup is separately extractable.
moderators_to_extract: Education setting and educational level (e.g., secondary school, vocational setting, college/university)
Participant age, mean age, and age range
Eligibility/risk criterion (e.g., current suicidal ideation, prior self-harm, suicide attempt history)
Intervention type, delivery mode, intensity, and duration
Study design, randomization status, and intervention-arm structure
effect_size_note: Use an effect-size orientation in which improvement favors the indicated intervention: because higher suicidal-ideation scores indicate worse outcomes, reverse the sign of continuous effects as needed so positive values represent a larger reduction in ideation with intervention. For multi-arm studies, retain every eligible indicated-intervention arm as a separate intervention-versus-shared-control row, record a common study/cluster identifier, and address the resulting non-independence in meta-analysis rather than merging arms or selecting one. Do not substitute later follow-up observations when immediate postintervention data are unavailable. For randomized trials lacking group-specific sample sizes, impute equal allocation across randomized groups unless contrary information is available and document the assumption for sensitivity analysis.
